=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- README.md
  Line or code reference: line 1456 (item 12e, the edited sentence)
  Problem: The README states the exhaustion comment will "post the remaining findings table (the same rows a fix issue would carry) in the `Project security pass exhausted` tracking comment" as an unconditional claim. The implementation at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4591-4604` is best-effort: it falls back to a count-only comment when rendering fails (line 4591-4593) or the table exceeds 60000 bytes (line 4600-4604). This is a documentation contract drift — the primary operator-facing document promises a table that the code may not deliver.
  Why it fails at runtime: An operator who finds `ai:security-pass-failed` on a tracking issue will open the exhaustion comment expecting a findings table, per the README. If rendering failed or the table was too large, they see only a count with no indication of what the auditor flagged — exactly the gap the changelog says this PR closes. The changelog fragment correctly documents the best-effort fallback, but operators read the README, not the changelog.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- README.md
  Line or code reference: line 1455 (item 12e, the edited sentence: "set `ai:security-pass-failed` and post the remaining findings table (the same rows a fix issue would carry) in the `Project security pass exhausted` tracking comment")
  Problem: The README states the findings table is posted unconditionally, but the implementation is best-effort with two fallback paths: render failure (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4591-4593) and the 60000-byte table budget guard (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4600-4604), both of which silently degrade the exhaustion comment to count-only with only a workflow `::warning::`. This is also the substance of the existing Copilot review comment on this PR (README.md:1455), validated here against the code.
